result:
Done. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed in the repo (verified with a local production build):

**Diagnosis:** The SaaS pivoted from "InboxZap" (email cleanup tool) to "Lumina" (AI meeting assistant), and the migration broke the site's SEO in several concrete ways — which is exactly what the GSC export shows: the only decent rankings are for the dead brand name "inboxzap" (pos. 4-8), while the historical content (email-cleanup topics, ~13k total impressions) sits at position 40-60 with near-zero CTR and no path to recovery since it's irrelevant to the current product.

**Fixes applied:**
1. **`app/layout.tsx`** — title/description/OG tags still said "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" while the page content is 100% Lumina. Corrected metadata, added canonical, and added `Organization` + `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD.
2. **`app/features/page.tsx`, `app/pricing/page.tsx`** — created; both were linked from nav/CTA but didn't exist (404s on core conversion pages).
3. **`app/page.tsx`** — added a real `#faq` section with `FAQPage` JSON-LD (nav/redirect pointed at `/#faq`, which didn't exist).
4. **`app/blog/page.tsx` + `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` + `app/blog/posts.ts`** — blog index was a client component fetching `/api/posts`, which doesn't exist, so it always showed "Could not load posts" with zero crawlable links, and there was no `[slug]` route at all. Rebuilt as server-rendered with 3 new posts on-topic for the actual product (meeting notes, meeting overload, async standups) plus `Article` JSON-LD per post.
5. **`next.config.js`** — the 12 legacy `/blog/post-N` URLs (still indexed, still getting impressions) had no route and would 404 on deploy. Added a 301 redirect to `/blog` instead of destroying that equity.
6. **`app/sitemap.ts`** — was missing `/features`, `/pricing`, and all blog posts (explicitly skipped via a TODO). Now includes everything real, with `lastmod` on posts.

Verified via `next build` + `next start`: all routes return 200, old post URLs 308-redirect cleanly, sitemap lists 7 real URLs, FAQ/Organization/SoftwareApplication/Article JSON-LD all render.

One unrelated item worth flagging: `npm install` warned that the pinned `next@14.2.5` has a known security vulnerability (patch available) — not an SEO issue, but worth upgrading separately.
